text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 11%. The drop follows the company's quarterly earnings announcement on November 5th and comes as oil prices have softened—US crude is trading at $99.64 per barrel, down meaningfully from where it likely was when the stock was $146 two weeks ago. Weaker oil prices directly compress profits for oil producers like ConocoPhillips, since their revenue depends on selling barrels at higher prices.

The broader headwind here is political: yesterday's midterm election results delivered a setback for fossil fuel interests, with voters rejecting Trump and GOP candidates who opposed renewable energy expansion. While oil prices remain supported by geopolitical tensions (Iran negotiations remain stalled), the electoral shift signals longer-term policy headwinds for traditional energy companies, which may be weighing on investor sentiment beyond just the daily commodity price move.
